# Threat model

Fixture. Two block quotes, wrapped differently from their copies in the policy,
with prose between them so the check has to end one quotation and begin another
rather than reading the pair as one.

## What a leaked link costs

The bound, and this is the sentence the policy repeats word for word:

> Somebody holding a leaked link gets one account for each use the invitation
> had left, with exactly the template it carried.

Every clause of it is a property some other issue has to make true.

## What a clone costs

The second bound, kept here so the clean case cannot pass by there being one
quotation on each side and nothing to tell apart:

> Two servers from one data directory both honour the same live invitations,
> because neither knows the other exists.

## What is not defended

Not read by this leg. It is here because the file the other leg reads is this
same file, and a fixture missing the section would refuse for its reason
instead of answering this one.

This paragraph is the opening rather than an item.

A leaked link within its validity is an account for whoever found it.

An operator with administrator rights can mint whatever the ceilings allow.
